interpretation: The official filing discovery/materialization/classification pipeline is technically viable at bounded scale: 20 of 21 selected filings reached classifier-ready output.
The bounded sample does not establish enough positive-event density to justify an expensive full 2023-2024 historical backfill under the frozen feasibility gate.
The density failure is not a classifier or technical failure: positives were found in three distinct quarters, but only three positive filings and two distinct securities were reconstructed.
No price or return data were consumed, so this phase makes no alpha, excess-return or investment-performance claim about E events.
The two 2023Q3 targeted Retry2 filings were both successfully reconstructed and classified NOT_ESTABLISHED; they do not rescue density.
The existing 2024Q4 embedded-text blocker remains fail-closed and was not rescued with OCR.

problem_elimination_pass.final_user_goal: Obtain enough causal evidence-event observations to validate an evidence-anchored Setup without paying for a broad historical filing reconstruction that the bounded sample does not justify.
hard_constraints: Do not treat E eligibility or an E event as validated alpha before outcome research is separately authorized.
Do not change the frozen E classifier, triage semantics or materiality rule to increase event yield.
Do not reopen full historical backfill under V2.8.11.
Do not resume open-ended pure-price entry-trigger discovery.
No Setup, First60, Episode or live authorization exists.
removed_soft_assumptions: A large historical backfill is necessary before any future evidence-anchored learning can continue.
Sparse historical reconstruction must be solved by expanding keywords or hand-picking windows.
Repeated retries of already-successful historical windows add useful information.

Delete: Do not launch a full 2023-2024 CNInfo backfill.
Do not expand the eight V2.8.11 windows after seeing sparse positive density.
Do not add search terms, relax classifier semantics, or manually select AI-looking companies to increase positive yield.
Avoid: Do not use price outcomes to choose which E-event types to preserve or discard at the data-collection stage.
Do not treat repeated positive filings from the same issuer as distinct cross-sectional validation evidence without explicit event-level design.
Absorb: Reuse the already-working prospective E observation ledger, issuer identity binding, effective-date resolver and daily/prospective collection infrastructure.
Reuse future qualifying filings as append-only causal observations rather than reconstructing the whole past.
actions.Substitute: Shift from broad retrospective reconstruction to prospective shadow accumulation of qualifying E events, including event identity/type/provenance and later outcome fields only after a separately frozen outcome-observation contract.
actions.Precompute_Reuse: Persist each future official positive filing once with content hashes and causal effective date; deduplicate by announcement_id and issuer/event identity.
actions.Optimize: Only after a minimum prospective event sample is accumulated should outcome evaluation, event-type stratification or technical-overlay incremental tests be authorized.

next_stage_constraints: First freeze what constitutes one prospective shadow E event and how repeated positive filings for the same issuer are represented.
Define append-only provenance fields and causal effective date using existing V2.8.4 authority.
Do not compute or inspect post-event returns until the outcome-observation contract and minimum sample rule are frozen.
Use automated prospective collection rather than repeated chat-driven polling where existing GitHub Actions infrastructure can absorb the work.
Do not authorize trading, Setup emission, First60 append, fold3 or fold4 access.
